items.stem: Which statement best describes 'intranet'?
options: A method of sending electronic messages, with attachments, from one user to one or more others; messages are stored on a server until read.
Email fields that send copies of a message to other recipients; BCC recipients are hidden from the others.
Real-time text communication between users who are online, often with presence information showing who is available.
A private network within an organisation, using internet technologies, that can only be accessed by the organisation's members.
items.answer: A private network within an organisation, using internet technologies, that can only be accessed by the organisation's members.
items.markingKey: intranet: A private network within an organisation, using internet technologies, that can only be accessed by the organisation's members.

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'report'?
options: A table is in 1NF when it has no repeating groups of attributes and every field contains a single (atomic) value, with a primary key.
A database that stores data in several linked tables, connected by relationships between key fields.
A primary key made up of two or more fields which together uniquely identify each record.
A formatted output of data from a table or query, designed for printing or display, which can group records and show summaries.
items.answer: A formatted output of data from a table or query, designed for printing or display, which can group records and show summaries.
items.markingKey: report: A formatted output of data from a table or query, designed for printing or display, which can group records and show summaries.

items.stem: Assertion (A): A linker translates high-level code into machine code. Reason (R): The operating system needs instructions specific to that device to control it. Which option is correct?

A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is false but R is true
items.markingKey: A is false: "A linker translates high-level code into machine code." is incorrect; R is a true statement.

items.stem: Lakeside College in Accra is creating a website for elderly users with limited IT experience. Describe two design features that would suit this audience.
items.answer: Large font, high contrast, simple layout, clear labels, no jargon, help instructions.

items.stem: Sunrise Bakery in Seoul is writing an acceptable use policy after finding personal use of work computers and copied work in reports. Explain what is meant by plagiarism and why it is a problem.
items.answer: Using others' work without credit; dishonest; work does not show the student's ability; may break copyright.
items.markingKey: 1 mark meaning; 1 mark problem. [1]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'style' and 'field'.
items.answer: style: A named set of formatting settings (font, size, colour, spacing) that can be applied to text in one step. field: A placeholder in a document whose content is inserted and updated automatically, such as a page number, date or file name.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: style correctly described; 1 mark: field correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [1]

items.stem: Zara at Palm Grove Hotel in Istanbul has written an algorithm but it gives incorrect results. Assess the use of dry runs and trace tables by Palm Grove Hotel to test algorithms before coding.
items.answer: Points for: finds logic errors early and cheaply; improves understanding; no computer needed. Points against / limitations: slow for long algorithms; human errors in tracing; cannot test all inputs; real testing on the computer still needed. Conclusion: dry runs are valuable for small, critical sections but should be combined with computer testing.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: finds logic errors early and cheaply; improves understanding; no computer needed. Against: slow for long algorithms; human errors in tracing; cannot test all inputs; real testing on the computer still needed. Conclusion may argue: dry runs are valuable for small, critical sections but should be combined with computer testing. [6]

items.stem:
A data entry screen for Silverline Couriers contains these fields:
1. a postcode / zip code of a fixed pattern
2. the number of hours worked in a week, which cannot exceed 60
3. a quantity ordered entered as a whole number
For each field, name a suitable validation check and describe how it would work.
items.answer: 1: format check — must match the pattern; 2: limit check — not more than 60; 3: type check — must be an integer
items.markingKey: 1: format check [1], checks that data follows a set pattern, e.g. two letters followed by four digits / must match the pattern [1]; 2: limit check [1], checks that data is not above (or below) a single limit / not more than 60 [1]; 3: type check [1], checks that data is of the correct data type, e.g. a number not text / must be an integer [1]. [6]

items.stem: Nova Telecom, a telecommunications company in Bangkok, is installing a computer system to monitor conditions in its storage rooms. (a) Name two sensors that could be used and state what each measures. (b) Discuss whether Nova Telecom should replace manual checks by staff with an automatic sensor-based monitoring system.
items.answer: (a) e.g. temperature sensor (temperature); humidity sensor (moisture in air); light sensor (light level); infrared sensor (movement). (b) For: continuous, accurate readings; works in dangerous places; staff freed; immediate alerts. Against: cost of sensors and installation; sensors can fail or drift and need calibration; staff may lose skills; reliance on power and network. Conclusion: automatic monitoring is usually worthwhile if readings are frequent or the environment is hazardous, with periodic human checks.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each sensor with quantity, max 2. [2] (b) Up to 3 marks for points on each side applied to the scenario; 1 further mark requires a justified conclusion. [6]

items.stem: Mateo is preparing charts for a presentation to the directors of Summit Engineering in Auckland. (a) Explain why a title and axis labels are needed. (b) Evaluate the use of charts rather than tables to present data in the reports of Summit Engineering.
items.answer: (a) They tell the audience what the chart shows and what the values and units are. (b) For: trends and comparisons are seen quickly; engaging; suitable for non-specialists. Against: exact values harder to read; charts can mislead with poor scales; tables are better for detail. Conclusion: charts suit summaries and presentations; tables suit detailed analysis — often both are used.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each. [2] (b) Up to 2 marks for points on each side applied to the scenario; 1 further mark requires a justified conclusion. [4]

items.stem: Noah is installing a network in a small office for Meridian Hospital in Jakarta. (a) Describe the role of a router and of a switch in this network. (b) Explain why a wireless access point might be added. (c) Explain one disadvantage of networking the computers.
items.answer: (a) Router: connects the LAN to the internet/other networks, forwarding packets by IP address. Switch: connects devices within the LAN, sending data to the correct device by MAC address. (b) To let laptops, tablets and phones connect without cables, giving mobility. (c) Viruses can spread; security risks; cost of equipment and technicians; if the server/switch fails many users are affected.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark router; 1 mark switch. [2] (b) 1 mark wireless devices; 1 mark mobility/flexibility. [2] (c) 1 mark point; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: In a database for MetroBus, the field Mark has the validation rule >=0 And <=100. State whether each value is accepted or rejected: 100, 0, 72, 150.
items.answer: 100 accepted; 0 accepted; 72 accepted; 150 rejected
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: 100 accepted; 0 accepted; 72 accepted; 150 rejected. [4]

items.stem: Hana, the IT manager of Atlas Museum in Istanbul, is reviewing the cost of software licences. (a) Explain two advantages of off-the-shelf software for this organisation. (b) Explain one risk of using proprietary software from a single supplier.
items.answer: (a) Cheaper; available immediately; well tested with fewer bugs; lots of support, training and user forums. (b) Vendor lock-in: the organisation depends on the supplier for updates and prices; if the supplier stops supporting it, the organisation must change systems.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each point, 1 mark each explanation, max 2 points. [4] (b) 1 mark dependency; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'intellectual property'?

Software that can be used free for a trial period, or with limited features, after which the user must pay to continue using it.

items.markingKey: intellectual property: Creations of the mind, such as inventions, designs, software, music and writing, which can be legally owned and protected.

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'HLOOKUP'?
options: Compression that permanently removes some data, such as sounds people cannot hear, to reduce file size (e.g. MP3, MP4).
A spreadsheet tool that finds the input value needed to make a formula produce a chosen target result.
A function that searches for a value in the first column of a table and returns the value in the same row from a specified column.
A function that searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns the value in the same column from a specified row.
items.answer: A function that searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns the value in the same column from a specified row.
items.markingKey: HLOOKUP: A function that searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns the value in the same column from a specified row.

items.stem: A trainee programmer at Harbour Bank in Lagos is learning to test algorithms by hand. Explain why the algorithm should be tested with more than one set of data.
items.answer: Different paths through the algorithm (e.g. each branch of an IF, boundary values) need checking.
items.markingKey: 1 mark different paths; 1 mark boundary/invalid values. [1]

items.stem: Distinguish between 'open-source software' and 'custom-written software'.
items.answer: open-source software: Software whose source code is made available so that users can study, modify and redistribute it, usually free of charge. custom-written software: Software written specially to meet the exact requirements of one client or organisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: open-source software correctly described; 1 mark: custom-written software correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [1]

items.stem: Riverside Medical Centre, a medical centre in Bogotá, has set up an online shop where customers pay by card. (a) Explain why the data should be encrypted. (b) Describe how asymmetric encryption would be used to send the data securely. (c) Describe the purpose of a digital certificate.
items.answer: (a) The data may be intercepted while travelling across the internet; encryption makes it unreadable without the key, protecting confidentiality. (b) The sender obtains the receiver's public key and uses it to encrypt the data; only the receiver's private key can decrypt it. (c) It authenticates the server by linking its identity to its public key, signed by a trusted certificate authority.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark interception risk; 1 mark unreadable without key. [2] (b) 1 mark public key of receiver encrypts; 1 mark private key decrypts. [2] (c) 1 mark authentication/identity; 1 mark issued/signed by CA. [2]

items.stem: Delta Water Utility in Nairobi keeps its records in a relational database and managers want regular reports. (a) Explain what is meant by a calculated field, giving an example. (b) Describe how a report can group and summarise data. (c) Explain why parameter queries are useful.
items.answer: (a) A field computed from other fields, e.g. Total: [Price]*[Quantity]. (b) Records grouped by a field (e.g. Region) with group headers; subtotals, counts or averages in group footers; grand total in report footer. (c) The user enters the criterion when the query runs (e.g. a date), so one query can be reused for different values.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark meaning; 1 mark example. [2] (b) 1 mark grouping; 1 mark summary functions. [2] (c) 1 mark prompt for value; 1 mark reuse. [2]

items.stem: The council in Accra and Northfield Academy are working together to reduce the digital divide and make online services accessible. Evaluate whether providing free devices is the most effective way to reduce the digital divide.
items.answer: Points for: removes the cost barrier immediately; helps students and job seekers. Points against / limitations: devices are useless without connectivity and skills; devices become outdated; may be sold; infrastructure and training may have more lasting impact. items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks limited points; 3-5 marks developed points on both sides applied to the scenario; 6-8 marks balanced, well-applied discussion with a reasoned conclusion. Indicative content — for: removes the cost barrier immediately; helps students and job seekers. Against: devices are useless without connectivity and skills; devices become outdated; may be sold; infrastructure and training may have more lasting impact. Conclusion may argue: a combined programme of infrastructure, devices and skills training is more effective than devices alone. [8]

items.stem: The council in Singapore has asked Palm Grove Hotel to install microprocessor-controlled traffic lights at a busy junction. (a) Explain two advantages of computer control over manual control here. (b) Discuss whether Palm Grove Hotel benefits more than it loses from using microprocessor-controlled systems.
items.answer: (a) Responds faster; works 24 hours; more accurate/consistent conditions; saves energy and labour costs. items.stem: Silverline Couriers in Istanbul is producing podcasts and short videos for its website. (a) Explain why the final video should be compressed before uploading. (b) Explain the difference between lossy and lossless compression.

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'symmetric encryption' and 'asymmetric encryption'.
items.answer: symmetric encryption: Encryption in which the same secret key is used both to encrypt and to decrypt the data. asymmetric encryption: Encryption that uses a pair of keys: a public key to encrypt data and the matching private key, kept secret by its owner, to decrypt it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: symmetric encryption correctly described; 1 mark: asymmetric encryption correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem:
This algorithm controls a compressor in a cold store. Temp is the temperature in °C. At the start, Compressor is "ON".
REPEAT
    INPUT Temp
    IF Temp > -16 THEN
        Compressor ← "ON"
    ELSE
        IF Temp < -20 THEN
            Compressor ← "OFF"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT Compressor
UNTIL SystemOff = TRUE
The inputs for Temp are: -13, -17, -20, -23, -21. Complete a trace table showing the value output after each input. Explain why the output does not change when Temp is between -20 and -16.
items.answer: ON; ON; ON; OFF; OFF
items.markingKey: -13 → ON; -17 → ON; -20 → ON; -23 → OFF; -21 → OFF (1 mark each); between -20 and -16 neither condition is true so the variable keeps its previous value (prevents rapid switching) [1]. [6]

items.stem: GreenLeaf Pharmacy in Nairobi uses a spreadsheet to calculate invoice totals including tax. (a) Explain the difference between relative and absolute cell references. (b) Evaluate the use of lookup functions instead of nested IF functions in the spreadsheets of GreenLeaf Pharmacy.
items.answer: (a) Relative references change when copied; absolute references ($) stay the same. (b) For: lookup tables are easier to read and update; handle many bands; fewer errors. Against: nested IF needs no separate table; lookup errors if the table is unsorted or the range is not absolute; #N/A errors need handling. Conclusion: lookups are better for many categories that may change; nested IF suits two or three fixed outcomes.

items.stem: Horizon Travel, a travel agency in Riyadh, sells its own software and is making a promotional video using music and images found online. (a) Describe what copyright legislation allows the owner to control. (b) Explain why the material found online cannot simply be used. (c) Describe two methods used to prevent illegal copying of software.
items.answer: (a) Copying, distributing, adapting, performing, renting or broadcasting the work. (b) It is protected by copyright; permission/licence is needed or it must be royalty-free/Creative Commons with attribution. (c) Product keys/activation; dongles; digital rights management; holograms on packaging; online licence checks.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per right, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark copyright; 1 mark need permission/licence. [2] (c) 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Nadia is normalising the database of SkyLink Airways in Dubai and writing a data dictionary. Evaluate whether SkyLink Airways should always normalise its database to third normal form.
items.answer: Points for: removes redundancy and anomalies; consistent data; easier maintenance. Points against / limitations: more tables and joins; slower queries for reporting; more complex design; small databases may not benefit. Conclusion: 3NF is usually best for operational databases, though some denormalisation may be acceptable for reporting.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks limited points; 3-5 marks developed points on both sides applied to the scenario; 6-8 marks balanced, well-applied discussion with a reasoned conclusion. Indicative content — for: removes redundancy and anomalies; consistent data; easier maintenance. Against: more tables and joins; slower queries for reporting; more complex design; small databases may not benefit. Conclusion may argue: 3NF is usually best for operational databases, though some denormalisation may be acceptable for reporting. [8]

items.stem: Riverside Medical Centre, a medical centre in Karachi, needs new software to manage its customer bookings and payments. Discuss the use of open-source software by Riverside Medical Centre.
items.answer: Points for: no licence cost; adaptable; large communities; not tied to one supplier. Points against / limitations: support can be limited; training costs; compatibility issues; may need in-house expertise. Conclusion: suitable if the organisation has technical staff or a support contract.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: no licence cost; adaptable; large communities; not tied to one supplier. Against: support can be limited; training costs; compatibility issues; may need in-house expertise. Conclusion may argue: suitable if the organisation has technical staff or a support contract. [6]

items.stem: Orbit Games Studio, a games studio in Hanoi, is installing a computer system to monitor conditions in its storage rooms. (a) Explain why an analogue-to-digital converter is needed. (b) Give two advantages of using sensors rather than human readings. (c) Describe what is meant by an actuator and give an example.
items.answer: (a) Sensors produce continuous analogue signals; the computer can only process digital data. (b) Readings taken 24 hours a day; more accurate; at exact intervals; in dangerous places; staff freed for other work. (c) An output device that performs a physical action in response to a signal, e.g. motor, valve, pump, heater switch.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark analogue output; 1 mark computer needs digital. [2] (b) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (c) 1 mark description; 1 mark example. [2]

items.stem: City Central Library in Jakarta has received complaints from office staff about aches and pains. (a) Identify two health problems that can be caused by using computers for long periods. (b) For one health problem, describe its cause and how it can be prevented.
items.answer: (a) RSI; eye strain; back/neck problems; headaches; poor circulation. (b) e.g. RSI caused by repetitive typing; prevented by breaks, wrist rests, ergonomic keyboard.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark cause; 1 mark prevention. [2]

items.stem: Students at TransGlobal Logistics in Riyadh are learning to show algorithms as flowcharts. Assess the use of flowcharts rather than pseudocode to plan programs at TransGlobal Logistics.
items.answer: Points for: visual and easy for non-programmers; shows decisions and loops clearly; language independent. Points against / limitations: large algorithms become very big and hard to edit; time-consuming to draw; pseudocode is closer to real code. Conclusion: flowcharts suit small algorithms and communication with non-programmers; pseudocode suits larger ones.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: visual and easy for non-programmers; shows decisions and loops clearly; language independent. Against: large algorithms become very big and hard to edit; time-consuming to draw; pseudocode is closer to real code. Conclusion may argue: flowcharts suit small algorithms and communication with non-programmers; pseudocode suits larger ones. [4]

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'operating system'?
options: System software that combines separately compiled modules (object code) and library routines into a single executable program.
A large, powerful computer used by organisations to process very large volumes of transactions and data reliably for many users at the same time.
System software that manages the computer's hardware and software resources and provides an interface for the user.
An interface that uses windows, icons, menus and a pointer (WIMP) so the user can interact by pointing and clicking or touching.
items.answer: System software that manages the computer's hardware and software resources and provides an interface for the user.
items.markingKey: operating system: System software that manages the computer's hardware and software resources and provides an interface for the user.

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'email'?
options: Real-time text communication between users who are online, often with presence information showing who is available.
Connects devices within a LAN and sends data only to the device it is addressed to, using MAC addresses.
A method of sending electronic messages, with attachments, from one user to one or more others; messages are stored on a server until read.
Part of an organisation's intranet that authorised outside users, such as suppliers or customers, can access over the internet.
items.answer: A method of sending electronic messages, with attachments, from one user to one or more others; messages are stored on a server until read.
items.markingKey: email: A method of sending electronic messages, with attachments, from one user to one or more others; messages are stored on a server until read.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Trace tables are used during a dry run. Reason (R): The code follows the syntax rules of the language. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: Which word-processing feature should be used to show readers where each chapter starts in a 60-page manual?
options: An index
Track changes
Automatic page numbering fields
A table of contents
items.answer: A table of contents
items.markingKey: a table of contents: it is generated automatically from heading styles and can be updated when page numbers change.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Location tagging on public posts can be dangerous. Reason (R): Antivirus software makes it safe to open any attachment. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "Antivirus software makes it safe to open any attachment." is incorrect.

items.stem: The council in Riyadh and Starlight Cinemas are working together to reduce the digital divide and make online services accessible. Describe two initiatives that could reduce the digital divide.
items.answer: Rural broadband investment; free public internet access points; subsidised devices; digital skills training; low-cost data plans.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'site licence' and 'open-source licence'.
items.answer: site licence: A licence that allows software to be used on any number of computers at one site or within one organisation for a single fee. open-source licence: A licence that makes the source code available so it can be studied, modified and shared under the licence terms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: site licence correctly described; 1 mark: open-source licence correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Jonas uses a spreadsheet model at Nova Telecom in Singapore to plan staffing and costs for an event. (a) Explain one limitation of the model. (b) Evaluate the use of spreadsheet models by Nova Telecom to make financial decisions.
items.answer: (a) It relies on assumptions and estimates, e.g. demand, which may be wrong. (b) For: quick what-if testing; no real-world risk; goal seek and scenarios support planning. Against: models depend on assumptions and accurate data; errors in formulae; may give false confidence. Conclusion: models are valuable decision aids if assumptions are tested and results are used with judgement.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark point; 1 mark explanation. [2] (b) Up to 2 marks for points on each side applied to the scenario; 1 further mark requires a justified conclusion. [4]

items.stem: City Central Library in Madrid keeps its records in a relational database and managers want regular reports. (a) Explain what is meant by a calculated field, giving an example. (b) Describe how a report can group and summarise data. (c) Explain the effect of using a wildcard in a search criterion.
items.answer: (a) A field computed from other fields, e.g. Total: [Price]*[Quantity]. (b) Records grouped by a field (e.g. Region) with group headers; subtotals, counts or averages in group footers; grand total in report footer. (c) It matches any characters, so partial matches such as all names starting with "A" are found.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark meaning; 1 mark example. [2] (b) 1 mark grouping; 1 mark summary functions. [2] (c) 1 mark matches any characters; 1 mark example. [2]

items.stem: The council in Dhaka has asked Horizon Travel to install microprocessor-controlled traffic lights at a busy junction. (a) Describe how the microprocessor uses the sensor readings to control the system. (b) Explain how feedback is used in this system. (c) Explain two advantages of computer control over manual control here.
items.answer: (a) Reading converted by ADC; compared with preset value; if outside range a signal is sent to the actuator; loop repeats continuously. (b) The action of the actuator changes the conditions, which are measured again and affect the next decision, keeping conditions close to the preset value. (c) Responds faster; works 24 hours; more accurate/consistent conditions; saves energy and labour costs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per step, max 4. [4] (b) 1 mark output affects input; 1 mark continuous adjustment. [2] (c) 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets, a supermarket chain in Muscat, collects data about its customers during each month and sends out invoices in one run. (a) Explain why the old master file is kept after the update. (b) Discuss whether BlueWave Supermarkets should replace its overnight batch processing with online processing.
items.answer: (a) If the new master is lost or corrupted, it can be recreated by running the old master with the transaction file again (backup / recovery). (b) For: files always up to date; customers see current information; errors found immediately. Against: more expensive hardware and continuous availability needed; heavier load at peak times; batch is efficient for large regular jobs such as bills. Conclusion: a mixed approach is usual: online for transactions customers see, batch for large periodic jobs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark backup; 1 mark recreated from old master + transactions. [2] (b) Up to 2 marks for points on each side applied to the scenario; 1 further mark requires a justified conclusion. [4]

items.stem: Jonas, the IT manager of Orbit Games Studio in Kuala Lumpur, is reviewing the cost of software licences. (a) Explain two advantages of off-the-shelf software for this organisation. (b) Describe what is meant by open-source software.
items.answer: (a) Cheaper; available immediately; well tested with fewer bugs; lots of support, training and user forums. (b) Software whose source code is available to view, modify and redistribute, usually free.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each point, 1 mark each explanation, max 2 points. [4] (b) 1 mark source available; 1 mark modify/share. [2]

items.stem: Noah is training staff at TransGlobal Logistics in Singapore to use the internet, the intranet and the extranet. (a) Explain the difference between an intranet and an extranet. (b) Explain one advantage of an intranet for the organisation.
items.answer: (a) Intranet: private to staff; extranet: gives authorised external users (suppliers, customers) access to part of it. (b) Information is shared in one place, up to date and only accessible to staff, which is more secure and reliable.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each. [2] (b) 1 mark point; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Students at Palm Grove Hotel in Bangkok are learning to show algorithms as flowcharts. (a) Draw the flowchart symbol used for a decision and state what it contains. (b) State which symbol would be used for "OUTPUT Bonus" and for "Bonus ← Salary * 0.05".
items.answer: (a) A diamond containing a question/condition with Yes and No exits. (b) Parallelogram (input/output); rectangle (process).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark diamond; 1 mark question with two exits. [2] (b) 1 mark each. [2]

items.stem: Which term is described here? "How easily a product can be used by people with different abilities, including people with disabilities."
options: accessibility
digital divide
audience appreciation
digital literacy
items.answer: accessibility
items.markingKey: This describes accessibility.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Settings on social media or apps that control who can see a user's posts and personal information."
options: ergonomics
eye strain
privacy settings
data controller
items.answer: privacy settings
items.markingKey: This describes privacy settings.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Increasing the sample rate improves sound quality. Reason (R): No data is permanently removed. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: A video call uses 600 kbps (1 kbps = 1000 bits per second). How many megabytes of data are sent in 60 minutes (1 MB = 1 000 000 bytes)?
options: 270 MB
4.5 MB
items.answer: 270 MB

items.stem: Assertion (A): Freeware cannot legally be sold by the user. Reason (R): Shareware never has to be paid for. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "Shareware never has to be paid for." is incorrect.

items.stem: A galaxy-formation model needs 4 × 10^18 floating-point operations. A supercomputer runs at 8 TFLOPS (1 TFLOPS = 10^12 FLOPS). Calculate how long the task takes.
items.answer: 500,000 seconds (5.8 days)

items.stem: Distinguish between 'decision symbol' and 'flowchart'.
items.answer: decision symbol: A diamond-shaped flowchart symbol containing a question with two exits, such as Yes and No. flowchart: A diagram that represents an algorithm using standard symbols connected by flow lines.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: decision symbol correctly described; 1 mark: flowchart correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: A hospital ward run by City Central Library in Madrid uses sensors to monitor patients after surgery. Evaluate whether computerised patient monitoring can replace regular checks by nurses.
items.answer: Points for: continuous accurate readings; immediate alarms; nurses freed for other care; data stored for trends. Points against / limitations: false alarms and alarm fatigue; sensors detach or fail; patients need human care and observation of symptoms sensors cannot measure. Conclusion: monitoring supports but cannot fully replace nurses.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: continuous accurate readings; immediate alarms; nurses freed for other care; data stored for trends. Against: false alarms and alarm fatigue; sensors detach or fail; patients need human care and observation of symptoms sensors cannot measure. Conclusion may argue: monitoring supports but cannot fully replace nurses. [6]

items.stem: Felix is creating a new set of templates for Eagles Sports Club in Colombo. (a) Describe what is meant by a house style. (b) Explain two benefits of using templates.
items.answer: (a) Rules for fonts, colours, logo, layout so that documents are consistent. (b) Saves time; consistent house style; fewer mistakes; easier for new staff.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark rules; 1 mark consistency. [2] (b) 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Hana is using information from several websites to plan a business trip from Cape Town to Hanoi. Evaluate how far the quality of the information affects the decisions made by Northfield Academy.
items.answer: Points for: accurate, relevant, current and complete information leads to better decisions and fewer costly mistakes. Points against / limitations: managers' experience (knowledge) also matters; sometimes decisions must be made quickly with imperfect information; collecting perfect information is expensive. Conclusion: quality is critical, but the cost of improving it must be balanced against the benefit to the decision.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks limited points; 3-5 marks developed points on both sides applied to the scenario; 6-8 marks balanced, well-applied discussion with a reasoned conclusion. Indicative content — for: accurate, relevant, current and complete information leads to better decisions and fewer costly mistakes. Against: managers' experience (knowledge) also matters; sometimes decisions must be made quickly with imperfect information; collecting perfect information is expensive. Conclusion may argue: quality is critical, but the cost of improving it must be balanced against the benefit to the decision. [8]

items.stem: Sunrise Bakery in Jakarta is creating an online membership form linked to its database. Discuss the design of a data entry form that makes heavy use of drop-down lists and validation rules for Sunrise Bakery.
items.answer: Points for: fewer errors; faster entry; consistent data. Points against / limitations: lists can be long and slow to scroll; valid but wrong choices still possible; inflexible when new values are needed; rules can frustrate users. Conclusion: controls and validation greatly improve data quality but must be chosen carefully and kept up to date.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: fewer errors; faster entry; consistent data. Against: lists can be long and slow to scroll; valid but wrong choices still possible; inflexible when new values are needed; rules can frustrate users. Conclusion may argue: controls and validation greatly improve data quality but must be chosen carefully and kept up to date. [6]

items.stem: The council in Singapore and Summit Engineering are working together to reduce the digital divide and make online services accessible. (a) Describe two initiatives that could reduce the digital divide. (b) Describe two accessibility features that should be included. (c) Explain why training is needed as well as providing equipment.
items.answer: (a) Rural broadband investment; free public internet access points; subsidised devices; digital skills training; low-cost data plans. (b) Alt text for images; captions; resizable text; high contrast; keyboard navigation; compatibility with screen readers; voice input. (c) People without digital skills or confidence will not use equipment effectively, so access alone does not close the divide.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (c) 1 mark skills gap; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem:
For each situation, identify the data protection principle that has been broken and suggest what the organisation should have done.
1. An employee leaves an unencrypted laptop containing customer records on a train.
2. A company sends its customer database to a country with no data protection laws.
items.answer: 1: Personal data must be kept secure; 2: Personal data must not be transferred to countries without adequate protection
items.markingKey: 1: Personal data must be kept secure [1] + suitable corrective action [1]; 2: Personal data must not be transferred to countries without adequate protection [1] + suitable corrective action [1]. [4]
